meta.title: ky · fix uppercase retry.methods
meta.overview: A one-commit fix in sindresorhus/ky with a satisfying cause. retry.methods is documented in lowercase, and the retry check at Ky.ts:321 lowercases the request method before comparing — but the caller's array was passed through untouched. So retry: {methods: ['GET']} silently disabled retries: ['GET'].includes('get') is false, and the request threw on first failure instead of retrying. The fix normalises caller-supplied methods to lowercase during option normalisation, widens the type from string[] to Array<LiteralUnion<HttpMethod, string>> so known methods autocomplete without rejecting custom ones, and adds a test asserting 4 requests (1 + 3 retries) for methods: ['GET'].

files.why: Where the fix lives. normalizeRetryOptions already merged caller options over defaults; it now lowercases a caller-supplied methods array so the downstream comparison can match.
Types the retry option bag. methods was string[], which gave no autocomplete and implied any string was equally expected; it is now a LiteralUnion of the known HTTP methods plus string.
Adds the regression test. Counts requests against a server that always returns 408, so it fails if uppercase methods stop being retried.
Pre-existing. Normalises options in the constructor and owns the retry loop; line 321 is the comparison that the bug turned into a silent no-retry.

nodes.label: ky() factory
nodes.summary: The public entry point. Every request starts here and is handed to Ky.create with the caller's options merged over any instance defaults.

segs.n: createInstance closes over instance defaults and returns a callable. validateAndMerge combines those defaults with the per-call options, so retry may arrive from either — which is why normalisation has to happen once, centrally, rather than at each call site.
The default export is a pre-built instance with no defaults, so ky(url, {retry: …}) is the path the bug was reported on.

nodes.label: Ky constructor
nodes.summary: Builds the internal options object. Every option is normalised exactly once here, which is what makes normalizeRetryOptions the single correct place to fix the casing.

segs.n: Note line 204 alongside 207: the request method is normalised by normalizeRequestMethod (which uppercases known methods), while the retry list goes through normalizeRetryOptions. Two independent normalisations of the same vocabulary, in opposite directions — that mismatch is the root of the bug.

nodes.label: normalizeRetryOptions()
nodes.summary: Turns whatever the caller passed as retry — a number, a partial object, or nothing — into a fully-populated internal shape. This is where the fix lands: a caller-supplied methods array is now lowercased so the retry check can match it.

segs.n: retry: 3 is shorthand for "three attempts, defaults for everything else". Note this early return skips the new lowercasing entirely — correctly, because there is no caller-supplied methods array on this path.

Shape validation for the two array options, throwing rather than coercing. Worth seeing before the fix: it establishes that by the time we reach the merge, methods is either absent or a real array — so .map below is safe without another guard.

Explicit undefined values are stripped before merging. Without this, {methods: undefined} would override the defaults with nothing and disable method filtering — so this filter is what makes the spread on the next lines safe.

The fix. Defaults first, caller options over them, then methods is recomputed last so it wins over the spread on line 50. .map(toLowerCase) makes ['GET'] into ['get'], which is what Ky.ts:321 compares against. The ternary matters: when the caller passed no methods, it falls back to defaultRetryOptions.methods rather than mapping over undefined.

nodes.label: defaultRetryOptions
nodes.summary: The baseline every retry config is merged onto.

segs.n: methods: retryMethods is already lowercase, which is why the default path never hit the bug — only a caller-supplied list did. Note the defaults deliberately exclude post and patch: retrying a non-idempotent request could duplicate a write.

nodes.label: retryMethods
nodes.summary: The lowercase list of methods considered safe to retry — the casing convention the whole comparison depends on.

segs.n: All lowercase. Since Ky.ts:321 lowercases the incoming request method before the includes check, lowercase is the internal canonical form; the fix simply makes caller input conform to it.

nodes.label: RetryOptions.methods
nodes.summary: The typing half of the change: string[] became Array<LiteralUnion<HttpMethod, string>>, so editors suggest the six known methods while still accepting any custom verb.

segs.n: Both imports are new in this commit — the type change is what pulled them in.

Line 29 is the change (previously methods?: string[]). The doc comment above it already documented lowercase defaults, so the type now nudges callers toward the same casing the runtime expects. It is a hint, not enforcement: LiteralUnion still permits 'GET', which is exactly why the runtime fix is the load-bearing one.

nodes.label: LiteralUnion
nodes.summary: The idiom that gives literal autocomplete without closing the type. A plain union would reject custom methods; a plain string would suggest nothing.

segs.n: BaseType & {_?: never} is the trick: intersecting with an almost-empty object keeps TypeScript from collapsing the union down to string, so the literal members survive for autocomplete while any string still assigns.

nodes.label: HttpMethod
nodes.summary: The canonical lowercase union of methods ky knows about.

segs.n: Lowercase, matching requestMethods in core/constants.ts (which has a type-level test asserting the two stay in sync). This is the vocabulary the retry list is now typed against.

nodes.label: #retry()
nodes.summary: The retry loop: run the request, and on failure ask #calculateRetryDelay how long to wait — or let the error through.

segs.n: The control flow that makes the bug invisible: #calculateRetryDelay either returns a delay or throws the original error. So a method that fails the retriability check surfaces as the plain request error with no indication that a retry was skipped — which is why methods: ['GET'] looked like "retries just don't work" rather than a config problem.

nodes.label: #calculateRetryDelay()
nodes.summary: Decides whether this failure is retriable at all, and if so how long to wait. The order of its checks is the retry policy.

segs.n: Attempt count first (cheapest bail-out), then non-Error throws are wrapped for consistency. The ForceRetryError branch deliberately returns before the method check — an afterResponse hook that forces a retry bypasses method filtering by design, so that path was never affected by this bug.
The comparison at the heart of the fix, shown in context: reached only for non-forced retries, and throwing here is what silently cancelled retries for uppercase methods.

nodes.label: method retriability check
nodes.summary: The single line the whole change exists to satisfy. It lowercases the request's method but takes the allow-list as-is — so the two sides only meet if the allow-list is already lowercase.

segs.n: this.request.method is uppercase by then (normalizeRequestMethod uppercases known methods at construction), so .toLowerCase() yields 'get'. Before the fix the allow-list was the caller's ['GET'], so includes('get') was false and line 322 threw. Both sides are now lowercase. Fixing it here instead — by lowercasing the list at comparison time — would have re-run the work on every failure and left options.retry.methods inconsistent for anything else reading it.

nodes.label: #calculateDelay()
nodes.summary: Computes the backoff for an attempt that has already been judged retriable. Unrelated to the fix, included because it is the other half of what the retry decision returns.

segs.n: Exponential backoff, optional jitter (boolean or custom function), clamped by backoffLimit. Lines 295–297 fall back to the unjittered delay if a custom jitter function returns something non-finite or negative — a small piece of defensiveness against user-supplied callbacks.

nodes.label: normalizes uppercase methods
nodes.summary: The regression test. Serves 408 forever and counts requests, so it fails the moment uppercase methods stop being retried.

segs.n: A local server that always answers 408 (Request Timeout) and increments a counter. 408 is in the default retryStatusCodes, so the status is never the reason a retry is skipped — isolating the method check as the only variable.

The exercise: limit: 3 with methods: ['GET'] — uppercase, which is precisely what used to fail. throwsAsync is expected even when the fix works, because all four attempts return 408 and ky eventually throws; the assertion that actually detects the bug is the request count.

requestCount === 4 is the real assertion: one initial request plus three retries. Before the fix this was 1 — the request threw immediately without retrying. A count assertion rather than an error-message assertion is what makes this test able to see the difference.

nodes.label: retry on 408 with methods array
nodes.summary: Pre-existing coverage, included to show why the bug survived: the suite already tested a caller-supplied methods array — but in lowercase, so it passed throughout.

segs.n: Same shape as the new test, and the reason casing slipped through: this asserts that a caller-supplied array is honoured, which it was — as long as it was already lowercase. The gap was never "is methods respected" but "is it normalised", and the new test is the one that asks that question.
